claim_scope: cells behind a depth return remain unknown rather than observed free in the ray-grid fixture
a one-cell coordinate shift can destroy occupied-cell alignment
treating unknown cells as free can mark a dynamically occupied path falsely safe
a departed depth return does not prove its old cell free without explicit clearing evidence
a free point centerline can become unsafe after sweeping a nonzero footprint
expired free-space evidence returns to unknown and blocks a conservative path
rasterizing the segments between sparse waypoints can expose an intermediate occupied cell that waypoint-only checking misses
half-open metric-to-cell indexing with floor rejects a point just below the map origin that truncation would falsely include in cell zero

code.config: standard-library v4 tri-state ray grid, half-open metric indexing, segment rasterization, evidence aging, and footprint actionability fixture

limitations: two-dimensional integer grid with three noiseless rays
hand-defined dynamic update, square footprint, and approach affordance rather than learned prediction
Bresenham interpolation over integer center cells rather than supercover, continuous pose interpolation, continuous collision checking, or dynamics
fixed binary-exact 0.5 m half-open grid contract rather than arbitrary decimal-resolution floating-point behavior or a ROS/Nav2 map implementation
no height, semantics, velocity uncertainty, continuous swept volume, or real calibration
